change.title: stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields

source.quote: Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

tasks.reasoning:
The repo locks stripe-node 22.0.0 (package-lock.json). 23.0.0 is the next major. It pins 2026-09-30.endive, removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, the ErrorType export and V2List V1-only fields. The repo verifies webhooks with constructEvent (server.js:336), so the removed function itself is not used. The main risk is the endive behaviour on the Checkout Session create call at server.js:289. The usage map does not show which params it sends, so the migration agent must check whether payment_method_types (or ui_mode values) are passed and drop them. The agent should also check whether any code references Stripe.errors types or ErrorType. Webhook event payload versions are set on the dashboard endpoint, so they are not changed by the SDK bump. Staying on 22.x keeps working, so this is not an outage, but it is the path to staying current.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- stripe:2026-09-30-endive-api-version (api-version): New API major 2026-09-30.endive carries breaking changes; pin it via Stripe-Version or upgrade SDKs (node 23, python 16, go v87), effective 2026-09-30. stripe-node 23.0.0 pins 2026-09-30.endive. The SDK upgrade is the API-version move for this repo, which builds its client at server.js:15 without its own Stripe-Version pin.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "As the first version in the Endive release, `2026-09-30.endive` introduces both breaking changes and new features."
- stripe:2026-09-30-remove-payment-method-types-checkout (field-removed): payment_method_types removed from Checkout Sessions create, and paymentMethodTypes option removed from Elements deferred intents (Stripe.js), effective 2026-09-30. This only bites once the client sends 2026-09-30.endive. If checkout.sessions.create at server.js:289 passes payment_method_types, the call starts failing. The parameter must be dropped in the same PR as the bump.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog/endive.md
  "We [removed the `payment_method_types` parameter from Checkout Sessions]"
- stripe:2026-09-30-other-breaking-endive (other): Other breaking Endive 2026-09-30 items (unsure which apply): BLIK decline codes, eventually-due requirement errors on Accounts, Failed Tax Calculation error, SEPA debit settings in Accounts, Payment Evaluation nullable scores, 3DS Data Share Only, dispute evidence page limit, India mandates, effective 2026-09-30. These are endive-only breaking items and mostly cover Accounts, Tax, BLIK, disputes and mandates, none of which the repo appears to use. Any residual effect on checkout, billing portal or webhook handling would surface only with the endive bump, so check it in the same PR.
  Source: https://docs.stripe.com/changelog.md
  "Returns specific decline codes for BLIK payment failures"

callSites.why: Stripe client construction. Upgrading from stripe 22.0.0 to 23.0.0 changes the pinned API version to 2026-09-30.endive.
checkout.sessions.create. Under endive, payment_method_types is rejected on Checkout Sessions, so verify the params and remove it if present.
billingPortal.sessions.create runs on the new API version; verify it still behaves the same.
checkout.sessions.retrieve: the response shape is now endive. Verify the fields the code reads.
stripe.webhooks.constructEvent is kept in 23.0.0; only constructEventWithoutVerification was removed. Confirm nothing else in the webhook handler relies on removed exports such as ErrorType.

record.prBody:
## stripe-node (npm) 23.0.0: pins 2026-09-30.endive; removes Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType export, V2List V1-only fields [Verified]

### Change

Bumped stripe 22.0.0 -> 23.0.0 via npm (lockfile updated). Removed payment_method_types: ['card'] from checkout.sessions.create in server.js. Added scripts/check-stripe-migration.js. The client has no apiVersion pin, so it now uses endive. The code doesn't use constructEventWithoutVerification, ErrorType, or V2List. The webhook uses constructEvent and reads only fields that are unchanged (customer, subscription, status).

Files touched:
- `package-lock.json`
- `package.json`
- `scripts/check-stripe-migration.js`
- `server.js`

### Why

stripe-node 23 pins API 2026-09-30.endive, which removes payment_method_types from Checkout Sessions create, so the call would fail unless the param is dropped.

> Removed the function `Stripe.constructEventWithoutVerification()` that was mistakenly added in version 22.5.0 of this package.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stripe/stripe-node/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| stripe-migration | fail (1) | pass | 0 |
| syntax | pass | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- stripe-migration, added by the agent: `node scripts/check-stripe-migration.js` (fail (1) → pass)
- syntax, added by the agent: `node --check server.js` (pass → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `stripe__stripe_check_params`: pass

The agent's validator claims (not proof; graded against the recorded calls):
- stripe__stripe_check_params: pass (POST /v1/checkout/sessions with the remaining params at 2026-09-30.endive: no problems)

Test of this change: `stripe-migration`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Webhook endpoint API version in the Stripe dashboard should be aligned to endive; not checked.
- Deploy runtime must be Node >=20; not checked.

### Behaviour changes

- Checkout now uses dynamic payment methods from dashboard settings rather than card only, so customers may see other payment methods.
- API version moves to 2026-09-30.endive for all SDK calls; response shapes were not checked against live calls.

---

review.summary: The repo never used the removed surfaces (`constructEventWithoutVerification`, `ErrorType`, V2List V1-only fields), so the bump itself needs no code changes. concerns.issue: Line ~291: removing `payment_method_types: ['card']` is not required by anything in the quoted changelog. Consider pinning `apiVersion` explicitly in the Stripe constructor so the SDK major bump does not implicitly change the API version.

source.quote: We’ll drop support for it in the September 2027 major release.

tasks.reasoning: The notice is filed against stripe-go, but its text also states that stripe-node drops Node 20 in the September 2027 major. This repo uses stripe-node, and its Node runtime version is not recorded in the usage map. ## stripe-go will drop Go 1.24 in March 2027 major; Python 3.9 (stripe-python) March 2027; Node 20 (stripe-node) September 2027 [Verified]

### Change

The repo already uses stripe@22 and `new Stripe(key)`, and it makes no use of removed APIs. The only gap was that it declared no Node version. I added `engines.node ">=22"` to package.json. I also added test/node-runtime.test.js, which checks the engines field and the running Node version.

Files touched:
- `package.json`
- `test/node-runtime.test.js`

### Why

The notice says stripe-node drops Node 20 in the September 2027 major, so the repo should declare Node 22 or newer.

> We’ll drop support for it in the September 2027 major release.

Source: https://docs.stripe.com/sdks/versioning.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| node-runtime | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 0

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- node-runtime, added by the agent: `node test/node-runtime.test.js` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider validators: none run.

Test of this change: `node-runtime`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container node:22-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- The Vercel project's Node version setting was not checked and must be 22.x. vercel.json declares none, and Vercel reads the engines field.
- I did not call the Stripe validators or exercise the three Stripe call sites: checkout.sessions.create, billingPortal.sessions.create and checkout.sessions.retrieve. No SDK code changed.
- No provider validator was run.

### Behaviour changes

- Installs now warn on Node below 22, and Vercel may pick a Node 22 runtime from the engines field.

---

preparation.reasoning: No checks were detected, and the package.json has no postinstall, prepare, build or codegen hooks that the checks would need. The only generation script is the optional generate-seo script, which isn't required for the checks to run. Nothing needs to be prepared.

review.summary: For stripe-node, this change is about the runtime only: Node 20 support ends in the September 2027 major. No Stripe call site needs to change, so leaving server.js:289/318/411 alone is correct. The diff adds `"engines": {"node": ">=22"}` to package.json and a test that checks that string and the CI runner's Node version. That is a reasonable declaration, but it does not move production off Node 20. npm and most hosts treat `engines` as advisory unless engine-strict is set or the platform reads it. The deployment runtime (Vercel/Render/Docker/nvmrc/CI matrix) is not shown or checked. The 'verified' grade overstates what the node-runtime check proves: it passes once the string is in package.json and the CI box runs Node 22+, which says nothing about where server.js actually runs.

concerns.issue: `engines.node >=22` is advisory for npm and many hosts. It does not change the production runtime. If the app is deployed on a platform pinned to Node 20 (via platform settings, .nvmrc, Dockerfile or a CI matrix), it will still run on Node 20 when stripe-node's September 2027 major lands. No such config was touched or inspected.

The test is self-referential. It asserts the exact string the diff just added and the Node version of whatever machine runs it. It is not wired into an npm `test` script (package.json has no test script), and it reads 'package.json' relative to cwd, so it breaks if run from another directory. It proves nothing about the deployed runtime or about the Stripe calls.

Small behaviour change beyond what is forced: anyone on Node 20/21 now gets EBADENGINE warnings, or install failures under engine-strict. That is likely fine since Node 20 is EOL in 2026, but it is a policy choice to call out. Also, the dependency stays on stripe ^22, so the Node-20-dropping major will not be pulled automatically. Nothing breaks until someone bumps the major.
The task title says March 2027, but for Node the quoted source says September 2027. The March date applies to Go 1.24 and Python 3.9. The timing in the PR description should be corrected.
